The Boston, Massachusetts-based biotech lost more than 30% on Tuesday after disclosing that it disagreed with the feedback it received regarding its plans to submit a Biologics License Application for tovecimig based on data from its Phase 2/3 COMPANION-002 study.

“While we continue to believe the COMPANION-002 dataset demonstrates clinically meaningful activity in a setting of clear unmet need, we believe the FDA indicating a new study demonstrating a survival benefit is needed likely significantly complicates the regulatory path for tovecimig,” Wedbush analyst Robert Driscoll wrote.

However, Driscoll slashed his price target on Compass
to $1 from $5, removing tovecimig from his valuation model.
